title: The edit guard returns, re-keyed to the `@mandate` that governs the edited path, with one owned hook group per authored `@hook`
summary: This reverses milestone 5's B11 retirement of the guard at the mechanism level. @inventarch/steward-hook: the guard entry (runHook, and the host launcher's guard mode, which passes its arguments through) also accepts `--root <absolute root> --hook <identity>`, and evaluateMandateHook(root, hook, event) and printable(text) are exported. In that mode, for every edit tool whatever the hook names, the input checks, path safety and managed-state protection of the existing guard run first: installation state, owned projection files and, while a hook or guard registration is owned, the two Claude settings files and the cache launcher are refused with IA-HOOK-PROJECTION-MANAGED; the retired steward rule for .ia/src/systems/<name>/ is not applied and is not a fallback. In both guard modes a win32 path naming an alternate data stream (a : after the drive) is refused with IA-HOOK-PATH-UNSAFE, and in `--hook` mode so is a file with more than one hard link wherever it is under the root, selected or not (a pnpm store link included), since another of its names may be selected. The named hook must be one admitted authored (band 100) `@hook` that hook generation declares (PreToolUse; Write, Edit or MultiEdit; one or more workspace-relative path selections written with /; a non-blank message). Otherwise the registration refuses, with IA-HOOK-DECLARATION-UNAVAILABLE, the edits under the selection last registered for it (which the hook ownership state records), or every edit under the root when none is recorded; it does the same, with IA-HOOK-MANDATE-UNAVAILABLE, when the workspace's records cannot be read at all (a descriptor the db cannot read, a lock rewritten with CRLF line ends). Each such refusal names only commands that work from a shell in that state: `ia host claude --root <root> --remove --apply --yes`, which removes the registration and restores editing and needs neither an admitting workspace nor readable records; where the workspace admits, `ia host claude --root <root> --apply --yes`, which registers its current hooks; and where it does not, `ia validate --root <root>`, which shows why, or `ia report --root <root>` while an authored `@mandate` is among what admission refused, since `ia validate` then refuses. When the hook ownership state itself cannot be read, which the removal refuses too, the refusal names that state's repair instead: delete the state file and every IA hook group in .claude/settings.local.json from a shell, then run the removal. A hook decides an edit only when its hook.tools name the event's tool and its hook.paths select the file; any other edit is allowed. Nothing is decided because it lies under .ia/src: a workspace protects its governing records by selecting them in a hook, such as `paths [".ia/src/**"]`. The actor is established first. An event carrying agent_id is a subagent acting as the composition.agent of the one authored `@agent-profile` named exactly its agent_type; an unknown subagent, a malformed agent_id or a subagent without agent_type is refused with IA-HOOK-IDENTITY-UNAVAILABLE at every path the hook selects, governed or not. Any other event, including a main session launched with --agent (agent_type without agent_id), acts as the default actor (composition.steward, else its single participant) of the `@workspace` ia position seats the path in. A selected edit is governed by the mandates @inventarch/runtime's governingMandates returns for the path and that workspace: those whose authority.covers claims the path, and those scoped to the workspace. With none it is allowed. Otherwise it is allowed when profileRefusal allows the author mode (Synthesis) for the actor, a mandate that names no participant binding every established actor, and refused with IA-HOOK-NOT-MANDATED, the hook's message and the next command ia position --seat <mandate> --shape governance. A main session whose default actor is ambiguous, or that has none while a governing mandate names a participant, is IA-HOOK-IDENTITY-UNAVAILABLE. A refusal of the main session also names `ia host claude --root <root> --remove --apply --yes`, which removes every hook group and needs neither an admitting workspace nor readable records. An admitted governing mandate whose authority cannot be read is IA-HOOK-MANDATE-UNAVAILABLE naming its governance position, unreadable records are IA-HOOK-MANDATE-UNAVAILABLE naming `ia report --root <root>`, and while any authored `@mandate` fails admission every selected edit is IA-HOOK-MANDATE-UNAVAILABLE naming that mandate's path:line and `ia report --root <root>` (described in the mandate-admission note; `ia validate`, mandate-gated, would refuse there), and a selected path reached through a link, a junction or a short name is IA-HOOK-PATH-UNSAFE. hook.paths and authority.covers are matched in the G06c dialect (only *, ? and / are special) with db pathKey applied to both sides, so on win32 and darwin, where pathKey folds case whatever the volume, DOCS/x.md is under docs/** and Docs/** (on a case-sensitive directory there, a sibling spelled in another case is selected or claimed too), and on other platforms case is significant. Refusal reasons are printed without terminal escape sequences, C0 or C1 controls, line separators or bidirectional controls, and bounded. @inventarch/runtime: HOOK_CODES gains IA-HOOK-DECLARATION-UNAVAILABLE, IA-HOOK-MANDATE-UNAVAILABLE and IA-HOOK-NOT-MANDATED; the package root exports evaluateMandateGuard(handle, within, request), mandateGuardSelects(request) and seatedWorkspace(handle, within, path) with the MandateGuardRequest and MandateGuardDecision types, and the ./internal/mandate-guard subpath serves the guard module; the ./internal/packet subpath also exports fieldsAt, valuesAt, textsAt and stated, the field readers the packet and the host generators share; GoverningOptions gains an optional fold key, and without it governingMandates is unchanged. @inventarch/distribution: the ./guard-registration subpath exports HOOK_TOOLS, hookStatePath, hookGroup, savedHooks, planHookRegistration(root, {cache, hooks} | {remove}), planHooksFor(root, expected, hooks), applyHookRegistration(plan, checkpoint?), readHookRegistration(root, id?), observeHookRegistration(root, id?), hookGroupDigest(group) and hooksDisabledBy(root) with the HookRow, HookTool, HookRequest, HookAction, HookPlan, HookState, OwnedHook, HookDrift and Group types. They keep one PreToolUse group per hook row {identity, tools, paths} in .claude/settings.local.json, whose matcher is always Write|Edit|MultiEdit (the row's tools are validated, and the guard applies them to the hook's paths from the record) and whose handler runs `guard --root <root> --hook <identity>` in the retired guard's fixed derivation. The groups are owned by exact match against .ia/distributions/hosts/claude-hooks-<id>.json (ia.hook-registration-state.v1), which also records each hook's registered paths; they are published under the host lock through guard-pending.json (format ia.hook-registration-pending.v1) and recovered by recoverGuardRegistration (recover-guard), which reads either journal format. With disableAllHooks on, a plan that would create or update a group refuses, and one that only keeps or removes owned groups proceeds. Unrelated groups, keys and bytes are kept; a re-plan of the same rows writes nothing; a changed cache replaces the owned group in place, a changed selection updates only the ownership state, and a changed tool list neither (the guard reads the tools from the record); and removing the last hook removes only its groups, the containers the first registration created and a file it created, so the settings return to their original bytes only when nothing else in them changed meanwhile, and a container the groups emptied that existed before is written as [] or {} whatever whitespace it held. An owned group deleted, changed or duplicated by hand is refused with IA-DIST-LOCAL-MODIFICATION, naming the way back: for a changed or duplicated group, delete only that group, then remove the registration (`ia host claude --remove --apply`) and register it again. guardNode takes an optional hook identity; assertRetirableGuard and the retired guard's removal ignore groups that name --hook, so a 1.x steward-guard registration is still only ever removed; and the launcher's guard mode description names --hook. Limits: how ia host, ia project and ia init register the groups is described with the projection writer's change; Codex hooks remain unsupported; excluded words are not enforced by the guard (record authoring enforces them); the guard reads records, not file bytes, and a mandate grants no host permission; Claude Code on win32 runs the direct form, which still fails open when its Node cannot start; the nine machine routes, MACHINE_PROTOCOL versions 1 and 2 and every ia scope form are unchanged.
